entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Hastings, fought on 14 October 1066, was a pivotal event in world history that saw the Norman Conquest of England. 

 Led by King Harold II of England and William, Duke of Normandy, the battle took place in Hastings, a small town in Sussex. The outcome was a decisive victory for William, who went on to become King William I of England, establishing the Norman dynasty that would shape English politics and culture for centuries to come. 

 The consequences of the battle were far-reaching: William's victory led to the displacement of the Anglo-Saxon aristocracy and the introduction of French culture and language into England. This, in turn, had a lasting impact on the development of English politics, language, and literature. 

 As one historian noted, 'The Norman Conquest of England was a turning point in the history of the English language, marking the beginning of a period of French influence that would last for centuries.'
